references.text: In [ref:5 Mos 14:29|Deuteronomy 14:29], God commands that the tithe be shared with, among others, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow – the poor and vulnerable in society. This reflects Jesus' call to invite those who cannot repay.

[ref:5 Mos 26:12-13|Deuteronomy 26:12-13] speaks of the tithe year when one gives to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow. God's people are called to care for the poor and marginalized, just as Jesus encourages here.

Job describes his righteous conduct in [ref:Job 29:15-16|Job 29:15-16]: "I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame. I was a father to the poor." This aligns with Jesus' list of those who should be invited to a banquet.

[ref:Ordsp 14:21|Proverbs 14:21] says that whoever shows mercy to the helpless is blessed. Jesus' call to invite the poor and outcasts to a banquet reflects this principle of blessing through compassion.

[ref:Ordsp 19:17|Proverbs 19:17] teaches that whoever shows mercy to the poor lends to the Lord, and He will repay them. Jesus' promise of repayment at the resurrection of the righteous (v.14) is parallel.

In [ref:Jes 58:7|Isaiah 58:7], God calls us to share bread with the hungry and bring the homeless and helpless into our homes. This prophetic text forms the background for Jesus' teaching on sharing a meal with the poor.

In the parable that follows in [ref:Luk 14:21|Luke 14:21], the master sends his servant to bring in exactly those same groups – the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame – to the great banquet. The parable illustrates the principle from verse 13.
[ref:Luk 14:14|Luke 14:14] is the direct continuation where Jesus promises that one will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous – the motivation for giving to those who cannot repay.
In [ref:Luk 6:35|Luke 6:35], Jesus says we should do good and lend without expecting anything in return. The principle of giving without expectation of repayment is the same as in 14:13.

[ref:Hebr 13:2|Hebrews 13:2] encourages us not to forget hospitality, for by it some have entertained angels without knowing it. Hospitality without ulterior motives is a recurring biblical theme that echoes Jesus' words here.
